newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen creeps higher, touches record high.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen creeps higher, touches record high.

text.p: The benchmark March three-month euroyen futures contract hit a record high of 99.28 by midday in Tokyo on Tuesday, propelled mainly by a late surge in Japanese government bonds (JGBs), traders said.

JGBs jumped just prior to their morning close on stop-loss buying prompted by remarks from Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso, who said reports from the United States earlier this month that had him saying it was possible Japan's official discount rate would be raised by the year-end were not entirely correct.
Aso said the interviewer did not refer to a time frame in his question and he only said it was possible the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would raise rates.
These comments sent the key September JGB contract to a four-month high of 127.16. It ended the morning at 127.14, compared to Monday's 126.95.
Euroyen traders were sceptical about the significance of these remarks, saying that the fact that the market rose on these was due mainly to a serious dearth of factors.
The key three-month March euroyen contract ended the morning at 99.28, compared to 99.25 at Monday's close.
The key contract moved from 99.25 to 99.28, with turnover a sparse 10,639 contracts.
"The thinness of the market definitely exaggerated moves a bit," one city bank trader said.

He added that while today's rise had perhaps cleared the way for a few more gains, heavy resistance at 99.30 was likely to hold until next week, when a raft of economic factors are due for release and an auction of 10-year JGBs is likely.
"Depending on next week's indicators in particular, we could very well break through this. But this week we don't have any real reason to buy actively," he said.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted a neutral money market operation by draining 100 billion yen from the market in its regular morning operation, with key overnight call money being traded mainly at 0.48 percent by late morning, traders said.
Around 20 billion yen of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.57 percent, the same as Monday.
